content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm having trouble with my [product_name] operator panel display. When I use the arrow and ESC keys on the [product_name] basic module, the counter increments, but on the [product_name] operator panel it doesn't work as expected. Does anyone know what could be causing this? Thanks, [user_name]
Could you please upload your program? That would help to analyze your issue.
I believe this is a hardware issue rather than a software problem.

Hello, Could you specify your [product_name] type, series, and the series of your operator panel? There is some related information in the German forum section. Sharing these details would make it easier to investigate. Best regards [user_name]

Hello, a) The ON-delay does not work with cursor keys on either the [product_name] base module or the operator panel because pressing [ESC] plus the cursor key only sends one pulse per cycle. One solution could be to use external keys or the F-keys. b) Are you using the cursor keys to navigate through [product_name] menus using the operator panel? c) On some versions of [product_name], pressing [ESC] plus cursor keys does not always work as expected. d) I have not found a description of your error in the German forum. Best regards [user_name]

It's strange because when using the cursor keys on the [product_name] base module, the counter works and increments as expected. With the operator panel, it only increments once or twice, then you see an underscore on the display and it's not possible to increment further (see attached image).

Hi, The underline means you have activated edit mode in the message box (by holding [ESC] for a few seconds). If this happens, press [ESC] again to return to normal display mode. Please refer to the manual for more details. In edit mode, you can use the left and right cursor keys to navigate variables in the textbox. Press OK to edit the value, then use up and down. Best regards [user_name]
I couldn't find this in the manual. Can you tell me what page it's on? Thanks,
Thanks, but when I press ESC, I'm in edit mode. However, pressing OK doesn't let me change the variable. Any ideas? Thanks,
Thanks, but when I press ESC, I'm in edit mode. Pressing OK does nothing, and I still can't change the variable. Do you have any suggestions?

Hello, There could be two reasons: a) The textbox properties may have "Protection active" enabled. Try disabling it. b) Some function blocks, like "analog amplifier," have a bug where values cannot be edited in the textbox. Best regards [user_name]
Where is "Protection active" in this picture? My [product_name] programming software is in English. Thanks,

Hello, The correct setting is "Protection active," but it’s not in the textbox properties. Make sure "Protection active" isn’t selected on the block you want to edit in the textbox, or in the [product_name] parameter menu at RUN mode. Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing inconsistent behavior when incrementing counters using arrow and ESC keys on the [product_name] operator device compared to the [product_name] base module. The issue is that the key combination functions reliably on the base module, but on the operator device, it triggers an unexpected edit mode (indicated by an underscore) and disables further increments. This has led to confusion regarding key functionality and frustration due to unclear documentation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the increment operation using keys to work consistently and reliably on both the [product_name] base module and operator device. They also want clear documentation explaining display indicators and key actions.
